newsitem.title: UK: Halifax, A&L off on profit-taking, technics.
newsitem.headline: Halifax, A&L off on profit-taking, technics.

text.p: Shares in Halifax Plc and Alliance & Leicester Plc dropped on Monday as profit-taking and technical factors cast a shadow over the debut of the former building societies turned banks in the FTSE 100.
By 0830 GMT Halifax was down 16p at 754p while Alliance & Leicester fell 12p to 591p.
Despite a sharp fall in UK shares overall, Halifax and Alliance shares surged on Friday as institutions loaded up with stock ahead of their FTSE debut
"There was a lot of buying before as funds were trying to build up stock. Now less people are chasing up the shares", an analyst said.
Apart from that, the price of Halifax was above the fundamentals, the analyst said.

"We think at this price it is significantly more expensive than Abbey National but we have yet to see a natural market in these shares (Halifax and Alliance & Leicester)", Ian McEwan, analyst at Lehman Brothers, said, adding trading in both shares had been affected by technical factors too.

The inclusion of Halifax and Alliance & Leicester increased the retail banking sector's representation in the FTSE 100's capitalisation from around 18.5 percent to more than 21 percent. Financial stocks as a whole currently have a weighting of 24.09 percent.
